summary: Latency regression: p95/p99 spikes tied to continuous batching (prod us-east-1)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (StellarDocs Inc.) reports intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional request timeouts for inference requests routed to dedicated capacity in us-east-1. Spikes started 2026-02-28 ~14:00 UTC and are correlated with increases in continuous-batching wait times observed on serving hosts.

Impact:
- Affected endpoints: text-generation and chat routes for models redwood/longformer-3b and redwood/seq2seq-7b.
- Customer reports user-facing latency spikes up to 3-4x baseline at p99 and several timed-out requests (HTTP 504) during spikes.
- Customer is on Dedicated capacity and relies on low-variance latency for synchronous features.

Environment:
prod, us-east-1, Dedicated pool ID: dp-us-e-17 (customer-shared reserved nodes).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send steady stream of small token generation requests (~10-20 tokens) at 200 qps to the customer's pinned model endpoint.
2) Observe p95/p99 latency using internal per-route dashboards and the customer's client metrics.
3) Note that spikes appear after periods of low request entropy when the broker groups requests into larger continuous-batch windows.

Observed behavior:
- p50 stable (~80ms) but p95 rises to 600ms and p99 to 1.2s during spike windows.
- Serving runtime logs show increased continuous-batcher wait_time and larger batch sizes being emitted intermittently.
- Some streaming connections drop with client-side 504s/timeouts when combined with network jitter.

Expected behavior:
p95/p99 should remain within SLO (p95 < 250ms, p99 < 500ms) for this Dedicated tier and workload. Continuous batching should not introduce high tail latency for small, latency-sensitive requests.

Temporary workaround:
- We advised customer to set request hint header "x-rw-priority: low-wait" (experimental) to bias routing to lower-batch-latency lanes (works for ~70% of requests).
- Suggested reducing client-side request bundling and enabling retry/backoff to mitigate transient 504s.
investigation_notes:
Initial investigation by support: correlated spike timestamps with continuous-batcher metrics from serving nodes in dp-us-e-17. Observed increased batch_wait_time on 3 of 8 nodes and higher variance in kernel selection latency.

Hypotheses considered:
- Regression in continuous-batching heuristics after recent scheduler change (see PR #482).
- Noisy-neighbor CPU/GPU scheduling on dedicated pool causing uneven kernel latency.
- Network jitter causing streaming response delays and triggering larger batch windows.

Findings so far:
- Canary of latest serving runtime commit (commit ab12cd3) shows a change to the batching threshold calculation introduced 2026-02-25; synthetic load reproduces p99 spike when combining low-entropy requests with that heuristic.
- Node-level GPU metrics do not show sustained saturation; spikes align with moments when batcher increases max wait before flushing by heuristics (intended to improve throughput).
- Linked issues SUP-4821 and SUP-10642 document similar regressions on other pools; patterns are consistent.

Next steps:
- Roll back batching heuristic change in a canary subset of dp-us-e-17 nodes and measure p99.
- Add additional logging around batch flush decisions and per-request wait_time buckets.
- Prepare hotfix PR to gate the heuristic behind an opt-in config for Dedicated pools.
resolution_summary:
Pending hotfix deployment. Workaround provided to customer (x-rw-priority header + client retries). Engineering to land PR that gates the new batching heuristic and roll out to affected Dedicated pools after validation.

Planned fix: revert/guard batching-threshold change, add telemetry for batch wait_time percentiles, and add safer defaults for Dedicated capacity (lower max wait windows for low-entropy workloads).

Follow-ups: schedule post-deploy SLO verification, update runbook with a command to temporarily disable the heuristic on a pool, and notify affected customers after fix rollout.
